title: Allocation hot paths and object pooling in Node.js
hook: High-QPS Node services allocate millions of short-lived objects per minute — JSON parse results, request context objects, and Buffer slices. Reducing allocation rate lowers GC CPU and tail latency.

blocks.text: **Hot path**: code executed per request at scale. **Allocation churn**: creating new objects/arrays/strings every call triggers frequent Scavenge. **Pooling**: reuse pre-allocated **Buffer** instances, pre-sized arrays, or plain objects cleared between uses. **Zero-copy**: `Buffer.subarray` shares backing store; `slice` may copy in older APIs.

entries.plainDefinition: High rate of short-lived object creation.
Reuse instances instead of new each time.
View same memory without duplicate allocation.

blocks.text: Redis protocol parsers and SQS message batch handlers that allocate fresh `Buffer` per byte range burn CPU in GC not business logic. Pooling and streaming JSON parsers (`JSON.parse` on whole body) are common fixes.

blocks.title: Measure before pooling
blocks.body: Pools add complexity — profile with --trace-gc or clinic doctor first.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Pooling without clearing state — data leaks between requests. Releasing buffer before async IO completes. Premature optimization without profiling.

blocks.text: Fastify and uWebSockets.js minimize allocations by design. Compare p99 with wrk load test before/after pool. V8 TurboFan inlines small loops — sometimes single for-loop beats functional chain allocations.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Pools everything without measurement. Releases pooled buffer during async send. Cannot name allocation churn.

interviewTakeaways: Hot path = per-request code at scale — minimize allocations.
Stream large SQS/CSV payloads — avoid whole-body parse.
60s: High QPS means GC matters. Pool Buffers, reuse context objects, stream files. Profile first. C# ArrayPool<byte> analog. Release after async done.
commonPitfalls: Weak: map/filter chain on 100k rows per request.
Weak: release buffer before async completes.
Strong: profile + pool + stream + correctness on release timing.
